subject.mainFocus: Project Definition, Record Profile architecture, source-aware documentation discovery, and Resource Registry reconciliation
subject.description: A reconstructed milestone work session that moved Klinswork from architecture design toward a working Project Definition exemplar, while reconciling Record Profile semantics, Viewer discovery, and Resource Registry routing.

narrative.promptingSituation: The session did not begin as a formally declared work session. Work emerged from continuing the foundations needed to make future structured sessions meaningful, then expanded into substantial architecture, documentation, Viewer, and Registry work.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The prior weekend had established Resource identity, Activities, Startup/context-routing direction, and a transitional Project/System model, but formal Project Definition had not yet been proven against a real Project.
narrative.intendedOutcome: No single prospective outcome was formally declared at session start. Retrospectively, the work converged on proving the first Project Definition exemplar and reconciling the documentation infrastructure needed to discover and route it.
narrative.approach: Reconcile ontology first; define record-family semantics; create a narrow Project Identity profile; instantiate Inventory Management; complete Project and System narrative/sidecar layers; test source-aware discovery in the Viewer; then reconcile stale Registry routing with Activity history.

progression.title: Ontology reconciliation
progression.description: Separated Parent/Child Project relationships from System level and reclassified Inventory Management and Task Assignment and Tracking as Projects, with Inventory 3.0 and Work Queue as Systems.
progression.result: A more durable Project → System hierarchy.

progression.title: Record Profile architecture
progression.description: Formalized Record Profile, Record Profile Library, Profile Template, Sidecar, Entity Record, Record Profile Registry, Schema Roadmap, and Authoring Template.
progression.result: Structured record types gained explicit semantic roles and authority boundaries.

progression.title: Project Identity profile
progression.description: Designed a deliberately narrow Entity Record profile for stable Project identity facts and left permanent Project ID allocation unresolved.
progression.result: Project identity became separable from name, path, hierarchy, Systems, Resources, and lifecycle.

progression.title: Inventory Management Project Definition
progression.description: Created the first Project Identity instance, local README, Project Summary, and Project Summary sidecar.
progression.result: The Project Definition architecture became a real exemplar.

progression.result: System meaning was documented while System Identity remained evidence-driven and deferred.

progression.title: Source-aware discovery
progression.description: Used Documentation Spaces and the source-aware manifest pipeline to discover Project and System sidecars.
progression.result: Projects source successfully reported two records.

progression.title: Local launcher reconciliation
progression.description: Updated the Windows batch launcher to refresh the source-aware manifest before launching the local Viewer and diagnosed a trailing-backslash quoting defect.
progression.result: Manifest refresh succeeded; launcher path normalization was identified as the fix.

progression.title: Online Viewer migration
progression.description: Updated the online static Viewer from legacy json-manifest/files[] discovery to documentation-viewer-manifest/records[] with manifestRelativePath routing.
progression.result: The online Viewer displayed the source-aware Projects tree.

progression.title: PST-SP template discovery
progression.description: Observed that a Record Profile template triggered the rich PST-SP subject preview even though the template's content fields were blank.
progression.result: Identified the need to distinguish Profile Templates from instantiated records in Viewer behavior.

progression.title: Resource Registry reconciliation
progression.description: Audited stale work-update-catalog paths, preserved legacy Resource identity where appropriate, registered the new source-aware Viewer infrastructure, and appended matching Activities.
progression.result: Current Resources no longer contain stale work-update-catalog paths while historical changes remain preserved.

problemsEncountered.problem: The first revised Windows launcher passed a Viewer-root path ending with a literal quote.
problemsEncountered.effect: The source-aware manifest refreshed successfully, but the local Viewer failed to start against the malformed folder argument.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Normalize VIEWER_ROOT and DOCUMENTATION_ROOT with `for %%I in (...) do set ...=%%~fI` so the paths do not end in a trailing backslash.
problemsEncountered.status: resolved in launcher design; local end-to-end retest remains part of later convergence work

problemsEncountered.problem: The online Viewer still used legacy `json-manifest.json` and expected `files[]`.
problemsEncountered.effect: The published Viewer could not consume the new multi-source Documentation Spaces architecture.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Update static mode to `documentation-viewer-manifest.json`, prefer `records[]`, use `manifestRelativePath` for fetch routing, and retain `files[]` as compatibility fallback.
problemsEncountered.status: resolved; online source-aware Viewer observed working

problemsEncountered.problem: The PST-SP Record Profile template launched the specialized PST-SP content preview and appeared empty.
problemsEncountered.effect: A profile template looked like a broken content record.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Diagnose the selected file as a template rather than an instantiated PST-SP sidecar; identify a future Record Profile / Template preview requirement.

problemsEncountered.problem: Resource Registry rows still contained obsolete `documents/work-update-catalog` paths and some stale descriptions.
problemsEncountered.effect: Current routing and architecture descriptions no longer matched repository reality.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Reconcile current paths/descriptions, preserve legacy manifest/builder identities, register new v2 infrastructure separately, and append Activities.
problemsEncountered.status: resolved for the audited current Resource rows

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Pass `%~dp0` directly as a quoted Viewer-root argument after assigning it unchanged to VIEWER_ROOT.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: It is a natural Windows batch idiom for the directory containing the launcher.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The trailing backslash interacted with quoting and caused the closing quote to become part of the Python folder argument.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Normalize directory paths before passing them as quoted command arguments.

turningPoints.title: Project/System hierarchy corrected
turningPoints.description: Inventory Management became a Project and Inventory 3.0 its System rather than perpetuating the previous transitional System/Application model.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Allowed Project Identity and Project Definition to be modeled at the correct level.

turningPoints.title: Sidecar and Entity Record separated
turningPoints.description: A sidecar was fixed as a machine-readable companion to a human-readable source, while Project Identity became an Entity Record.

turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Architecture moved from design to evidence-generating use.

keyDecisions.decision: Treat Parent Project and Child Project as the same entity type: Project.
keyDecisions.reason: Hierarchy is a relationship and should not be encoded as a separate identity type.
alternativesConsidered: Keep Inventory Management and Task Assignment and Tracking as Systems under one Housekeeping Operations Project.

keyDecisions.decision: Define Sidecar narrowly and introduce Entity Record as a separate Record Profile family.
keyDecisions.reason: A structured companion document and a canonical entity record have different authority roles.
alternativesConsidered: Use sidecar as a generic label for all structured JSON records.
consequences: Viewer discovery must learn Entity Records explicitly.

keyDecisions.decision: Leave Project IDs unassigned in the first exemplar.
keyDecisions.reason: Project Registry / Project Identity allocation authority is not yet settled.
consequences: Project Identity can be tested without premature global ID commitments.

keyDecisions.decision: Do not create System Identity yet.
keyDecisions.reason: The Project model should be proven before duplicating its assumptions at System level.
alternativesConsidered: Create a System Identity profile in parallel with Project Identity.
consequences: Inventory 3.0 is richly documented through README + System Summary + sidecar while SYS-### remains deferred.

keyDecisions.decision: Preserve legacy Viewer manifest/builder Resources and register source-aware v2 infrastructure separately.
keyDecisions.reason: The new manifest architecture is materially distinct, while legacy Resources remain historically identifiable.
alternativesConsidered: Repurpose RES-020 and RES-021 for the new files.
consequences: RES-020/021 become explicitly legacy; RES-044/045/046 represent the current source-aware infrastructure.

narrative.methodEstablished: Use exemplar-first architecture: reconcile semantic type and authority, instantiate one real Project Definition, test discovery and Viewer behavior, preserve failures and open questions, and only then derive reusable schemas/templates.
narrative.result: Klinswork now has its first working Project Definition exemplar for Inventory Management, a non-premature Inventory 3.0 System documentation layer, a source-aware online Documentation Viewer, and a reconciled Resource Registry whose current routes are separated from historical Activities.
lessonsLearned: Identity is stronger when it excludes mutable hierarchy, paths, Systems, Resources, and lifecycle facts.
A sidecar should remain a companion to a human-readable source; Entity Records need their own profile family.
Exemplar use reveals architecture requirements that are difficult to see from abstract schema design alone.
Discovery policy should be source-aware and configuration-driven rather than coupled to one physical folder root.
Stable Resource identity makes repository migrations historically intelligible.
Record Profile templates require Viewer behavior distinct from instantiated subject records.
The work-session structure becomes more meaningful as Project identity, summaries, routing, and discovery foundations become real.
narrative.directionChange: The Documentation effort shifted from designing Project/System record architecture in the abstract toward proving it with Inventory Management, then using the resulting records to drive discovery, Viewer, and Registry reconciliation tests.
narrative.narrativeSummary: An undeclared weekend session evolved into a major Klinswork architecture milestone. The work corrected the Project/System hierarchy, formalized Record Profile families, created the first Project Identity profile and Inventory Management Project Definition exemplar, completed Inventory 3.0 System documentation without premature System Identity, migrated the online Documentation Viewer to source-aware discovery, diagnosed a template-versus-instance preview issue, and reconciled stale Resource Registry paths with preserved Activity history.

general.summary: Klinswork now has a real Project Definition example for Inventory Management, clearer rules for different record types, a source-aware online documentation Viewer, and a cleaner Resource Registry.
keyPoints: Inventory Management is now treated as a Project and Inventory 3.0 as its System.
Project Identity is separated from README, narrative Summary, sidecars, relationships, and Resources.
The Viewer now discovers Common, Projects, and Therapy Documentation Spaces through a source-aware manifest.
Registry paths were reconciled without erasing historical Resource identity.

technical.summary: The session introduced the first Project Identity Entity Record profile and instance, completed a Project/System documentation exemplar, migrated static Viewer discovery from `json-manifest.json/files[]` to `documentation-viewer-manifest.json/records[]`, and reconciled legacy/current Viewer Resources with Activity-preserved Registry history.
keyPoints: Record Profile families: document-sidecar, entity-record, authoring-template.
Project Identity excludes mutable hierarchy, Resources, paths, deployments, lifecycle, and Systems from intrinsic identity.
Projects discovery currently finds Project/System sidecars but not Entity Records.
Online Viewer uses `manifestRelativePath` for source-aware static fetch routing.
RES-020/021 remain legacy; RES-044/045/046 represent the current source-aware manifest infrastructure.

projectSpecificLessons: Inventory Management is better represented as a Project than as the System itself.
Inventory 3.0 can be richly documented without prematurely freezing System Identity.
Project Definition benefits from separate identity, orientation, narrative, sidecar, System, and implementation-plan layers.
generalLessons: Identity should exclude ordinary mutable context.
A sidecar is a companion record, not a generic label for structured JSON.
Exemplar-first architecture produces higher-quality schema decisions than abstract freezing.
Discovery should be source-aware and independent of one physical repository root.
Stable Resource identity plus append-oriented Activities makes migrations reconstructable.
Templates and instantiated records require distinct Viewer semantics.
Historical terminology should be preserved rather than silently rewritten to current ontology.

recurringProblems.problem: Semantic identity becoming entangled with physical location.
recurringProblems.pattern: Paths and folder structure drift as the repository evolves, while conceptual Resources/Projects remain continuous.
